key_insight: QuasiMoTTo shows that test-time scaling does not have to rely on fully independent samples. By using correlated but exact quasi-Monte Carlo sampling, the paper aims to reduce redundant parallel attempts and make inference compute more efficient.
problem_solved: Language models often improve by generating many parallel answers at test time, but independent sampling wastes compute on near-duplicate solutions. This paper addresses how to scale inference more efficiently without sacrificing the benefits of exact sampling.
method: Designs a quasi-Monte Carlo sampling strategy for test-time scaling, replacing fully independent draws with structured correlated samples.
Preserves exactness while improving diversity across parallel attempts, reducing redundant computation.
Explores the sampler design space for efficient inference when many candidate solutions are generated per problem.
impact: For practitioners, this could lower the cost of multi-sample inference while keeping accuracy gains from test-time scaling. It offers a practical path to better throughput and efficiency in evaluation and deployment settings.
